items.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: I was never on that band for like year in, year out traveling. First I started subbing for a wonderful tenor player who passed away named Buddy Weiss.

ctx.x: Yeah. It seems like every few years another one comes along, where you had people doing that to “Alley Cat” and then the “Macarena” and some things never change I guess.

No I guess not. But we traveled. I was never on that band for like year in, year out traveling. First I started subbing for a wonderful tenor player who passed away named Buddy Weiss. He was a wonderful tenor player. But he had his problems with drug abuse. And he would get in trouble every so often and he’d have to leave the band and © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-
then I’d fill in for him. And then eventually he was not there anymore so I had the job. But then Ray wasn’t traveling all the time either. He was staying around and would just go out occasionally.
